{"world_model":"W5 (contrarian), after E036. Tip is E036: E035 plus the whitening-output detach after 20% of steps. It runs 5.314 s and scores 0.7532 on seeds 0–2, only 0.02 pp over the 3-seed gate. Its held-out mean is unmeasured, and so is E035's.

1. I mispriced the whitening detach. I predicted a 1–2% saving and E036 measured 2.4% (−0.13 s). The cheap-looking pieces on the 31×31 maps are not cheap: conv1's dgrad into 24 channels, the GELU backward on the whitening output, and the whitening wgrad. These ops are memory-traffic-bound, with fp16 activations of 2000×24×31×31, roughly 92 MB per pass. So the stem's large-map work costs more than its MACs suggest (H6.3), and the bandwidth story now has two hits (E028 and E036). Corollary: bandwidth-bound levers may transfer worse to the PCIe judge, which has lower HBM clocks and a lower power cap. The time ranking of kept levers may be partly SXM-specific.

2. "Math-identical" is not bit-identical (E035). Every edit re-rolls the numerics, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.15 pp. E035's +0.09 pp and E036's −0.16 pp are both mostly noise. Population mean of the tip: about 0.7530–0.7540. It has drifted down through repeated keeps at the gate (the winner's curse from gating on seeds 0–2 and 3–12).

3. What the code settles:
- Muon has no wd, renormalizes the filters every step, and runs 3 NS steps.
- The pool comes before BN, so group-1 BN runs at 15×15. Folding BN (I057) saves little.
- The freeze already covers group 1 plus the whitening bias.

4. The remaining stem dose is the freeze start at 60%. It saves about 9 ms per 28 px step and 10 ms per 32 px step, about 0.3 s in total (about 5–6%). It costs about 0.15–0.3 pp, because group 1 never adapts to the 28→32 jump. That rate is about the same as the epoch dial (about 0.13 s per 0.12 pp), so it is roughly neutral net.

5. Resolution: early low res is nearly free (E026, E033), and the 28/32 px tail carries the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).

6. Time-neutral boosters mostly lose (E025, E029, E030, E032). The airbench defaults sit near a local optimum.

7. Muon is worth about 0.4–0.8 pp. Its NS overhead is about 2–3% of time, so it should be kept.

8. Noise: 3-seed SD is about 0.15 pp, and the 10-seed SE is about 0.08 pp. Holding at a 0.753 bar needs a held-out mean of at least 0.7535, so the tip probably needs about 0.1–0.2 pp of epoch top-up before submission. Expected cost: about 0.1–0.2 s.

forecasts.reason: The ~35 extra truncated steps should save ~0.25–0.3 s (≥3%), but the held-out loss sits near the 0.15 pp bar, and the tip has no held-out margin to spend.
Same code, so seeds 0–2 should reproduce. Whether the pooled mean reaches ≥0.753 is about a coin flip given the downward drift from the winner's curse.
Group-1 BN runs on 15×15 maps after the pool, and frozen no-grad BN is cheap, so the saving is ~1%, below 2%. It also re-rolls the numerics.
E028 and E036 both show 31×31 stem traffic costing far more than its MAC share. Non-GEMM ≥30% and stem ≥35% are both likely.
Untuned SGD at batch 2000 on CIFAR-100 short runs loses ≥0.3 pp. Removing NS saves ~2–3%.

cruxes: What is the held-out (seeds 3–12, or fresh 13–22) mean of the E036 tip? If it is below 0.753, the next move must be an epoch top-up, not another cut.
What fraction of a 32 px step is memory-bandwidth-bound (I058)? This decides whether the stem levers keep their SXM-measured value on the PCIe judge.
Is the freeze dose (60% vs 75%) cheaper per pp than the epoch dial (~1.1 s/pp), or merely equal?
